title: Twenty years after 9/11, what have we learned about collective trauma? With Roxane Cohen Silver, PhD

sentences.en: This week marks 20 years since the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center and the Pentagon.
sentences.zh: 本周是2001年9月11日世贸中心和五角大楼恐怖袭击事件发生20周年。

sentences.en: Nearly 3,000 people died that day.
sentences.zh: 将近3000人在那一天丧生。

sentences.en: Millions more watched the planes hit the buildings.
sentences.zh: 数以百万计的人目睹了飞机撞击大楼。

sentences.en: Many saw the attacks on live TV.
sentences.zh: 许多人在电视直播中看到了袭击过程。

sentences.en: And two decades later, those images remained seared in the nation's memory.
sentences.zh: 二十年过去了，那些画面依然深深烙印在国家的记忆中。

sentences.en: Researchers call this kind of shared disaster a collective trauma.
sentences.zh: 研究人员将这种共享的灾难称为集体创伤。

sentences.en: For decades, they've studied how collective trauma affects individuals and communities' mental and even physical health.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，他们一直在研究集体创伤如何影响个人和社区的心理乃至身体健康。

sentences.en: Who is most at risk after a collective trauma event?
sentences.zh: 在经历集体创伤事件后，谁受到的风险最大？

sentences.en: How long do the effects of such trauma last?
sentences.zh: 这种创伤的影响会持续多久？

sentences.en: And after two decades, are we still dealing with the trauma of 9-11 today?
sentences.zh: 二十年后的今天，我们是否仍在应对“9·11”带来的创伤？

sentences.en: What did we learn in the aftermath of 9-11 that can inform our response to the COVID-19 pandemic, hurricanes, wildfires, and other large-scale disasters?
sentences.zh: 我们在“9·11”之后学到了什么，可以为我们应对新冠疫情、飓风、野火和其他大规模灾难提供参考？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学说话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Roxanne Cohen-Silver, a professor of psychological science, medicine, and public health at the University of California, Irvine.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是罗克珊·科恩-西尔弗博士，她是加州大学尔湾分校的心理科学、医学和公共卫生教授。

sentences.en: She studies how people cope with traumatic life events, including both personal and collective traumas.
sentences.zh: 她专门研究人们如何应对生活中的创伤事件，包括个人创伤和集体创伤。

sentences.en: She was the principal investigator of a multi-year study of the national impact of the September 11th terror attacks on the nation's mental and physical health.
sentences.zh: 她曾是一项多年期研究的首席调查员，该研究评估了“9·11”恐袭对全美心理和身体健康的影响。

sentences.en: She has also studied the short- and long-term effects of disasters, such as earthquakes, fires, school shootings, and war.
sentences.zh: 她还研究过地震、火灾、校园枪击和战争等灾难的短期和长期影响。

sentences.en: Most recently, she and her colleagues have been studying the COVID-19 pandemic and what she calls the cascading collective traumas of 2020 and 2021.
sentences.zh: 最近，她和同事一直在研究新冠疫情以及她所说的2020年和2021年层层叠加的集体创伤。

sentences.en: We'll talk about those today as well.
sentences.zh: 我们今天也会讨论这些话题。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us, Dr. Silver.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您能参加我们的节目，西尔弗博士。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: As I mentioned a few moments ago, you led several multi-year studies on the effects of 9-11 on Americans' mental and physical health.
sentences.zh: 正如我刚才提到的，您曾领导过多项多年期研究，探讨“9·11”对美国人身心健康的影响。

sentences.en: Can you tell us about that research?
sentences.zh: 您能给我们讲讲这项研究吗？

sentences.en: What were some of your chief findings?
sentences.zh: 您有哪些主要发现？

sentences.en: And what did we learn about collective trauma in the aftermath of 9-11?
sentences.zh: 在“9·11”事件之后，我们对集体创伤有了什么了解？

sentences.en: Thank you very much for that question.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您提出这个问题。

sentences.en: My colleagues and I began in the days after the September 11th terrorist attacks to study a large representative sample of Americans who were followed for about three years.
sentences.zh: 在“9·11”恐怖袭击发生后的几天里，我和同事们开始研究一个大型且具有代表性的美国人样本，并对他们进行了大约三年的追踪。

sentences.en: Those individuals were from across the United States.
sentences.zh: 这些人来自全美各地。

sentences.en: We had people, of course, who were from the New York area, as well as people in every state of the country.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们既有来自纽约地区的人，也有来自全国各州的人。

sentences.en: And we started a few days after the 9-11 attacks to ask people about their exposure to the attacks,
sentences.zh: 我们在“9·11”袭击发生几天后开始询问人们受袭击影响的程度，

sentences.en: whether or not they knew anybody who was in the World Trade Center or the Pentagon or on one of the airplanes,
sentences.zh: 他们是否认识身处世贸中心、五角大楼或某架飞机上的人，

sentences.en: whether or not they themselves were in New York City or Washington, D.C.,
sentences.zh: 他们自己当时是否身处纽约市或华盛顿特区，

sentences.en: whether they knew anybody who was presumably who was lost and presumably at that point killed by the attacks.
sentences.zh: 他们是否认识某位当时可能失踪、且在当时推测已在袭击中丧生的人。

sentences.en: And we also asked people the amount of television that they watched in the first few days after the 9-11 attacks.
sentences.zh: 我们还询问了人们在“9·11”袭击后最初几天里看电视的时长。

sentences.en: You may remember, or those who can remember that day, know that in general, most regular programming was suspended with a very intense media focus on the 9-11 attacks
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得，或者那些能记住那一天的人都知道，总体而言，大多数常规节目都暂停了，媒体高度聚焦于“9·11”袭击，

sentences.en: and the attempts to find survivors in the rubble and also to understand a little bit more about what happened.
sentences.zh: 以及在废墟中搜寻幸存者的努力，同时试图更多地了解发生了什么。

sentences.en: We followed these individuals in our study.
sentences.zh: 我们在研究中对这些人进行了追踪。

sentences.en: It was about 3,500 individuals.
sentences.zh: 大约有3500名参与者。

sentences.en: We followed them, as I said, for three years.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，我们对他们进行了为期三年的追踪。

sentences.en: And we looked at their emotional responses, their concerns, their ongoing concerns about terrorism.
sentences.zh: 我们观察了他们的情绪反应、担忧，以及他们对恐怖主义挥之不去的担忧。

sentences.en: And we also measured some of their physical health complaints, those physical health complaints that developed over the next three years.
sentences.zh: 我们还测量了他们的一些身体健康主诉，即在接下来的三年里出现的身体健康问题。

sentences.en: And in addition, during that period of time that we studied people, we assessed their ongoing, as I said, concerns about terrorism,
sentences.zh: 此外，在我们研究人们的这段时间里，正如我所说，我们评估了他们对恐怖主义持续的担忧，

sentences.en: but their continued exposure to personal traumatic experiences like did they lose a loved one to cancer?
sentences.zh: 以及他们持续接触个人创伤经历的情况，比如他们是否有亲人因癌症离世？

sentences.en: Did they themselves get sick?
sentences.zh: 他们自己是否生病了？

sentences.en: Did they witness violence?
sentences.zh: 他们是否目睹了暴力？

sentences.en: And we explored the impact of people's exposure to 9-11, the impact of exposure to other events in their lives,
sentences.zh: 我们探讨了人们接触“9·11”事件的影响、接触生活中其他事件的影响，

sentences.en: and how that impacted their psychological state over the next several years.
sentences.zh: 以及这如何在接下来的几年里影响他们的心理状态。

sentences.en: How did it impact them?
sentences.zh: 这给他们带来了什么影响？

sentences.en: What happened to these people over three years?
sentences.zh: 这三年里这些人经历了什么？

sentences.en: We were surprised to see the potent effect of media exposure on people's psychological and physical health over time.
sentences.zh: 我们惊讶地发现，随着时间的推移，媒体接触对人们心理和身体健康的强大负面影响。

sentences.en: We argued that individuals did not have to be directly exposed to the events of 9-11.
sentences.zh: 我们认为，个人并不需要直接接触“9·11”事件。

sentences.en: That is, they did not need to be at the World Trade Center or around the buildings to have been impacted by the events of 9-11.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，他们不需要身处世贸中心或建筑物周围，就会受到“9·11”事件的影响。

sentences.en: And these effects that you saw, they were higher than they might have been?
sentences.zh: 你所看到的这些影响，是不是比原本可能的情况更高呢？

sentences.en: Did you have a control that you were measuring them against?
sentences.zh: 你们是否有设立对照组来进行衡量？

sentences.en: Well, what we did was look at individuals who indicated that they watched the attacks live on television.
sentences.zh: 我们所做的是观察那些表示自己在电视上观看了袭击直播的个人。

sentences.en: So those who can remember those days know that the second plane hit the World Trade Center, and that was broadcast live.
sentences.zh: 因此，那些能记住那些日子的人都知道第二架飞机撞击了世贸中心，那是进行直播的。

sentences.en: And individuals could also see the buildings fall live on television.
sentences.zh: 个人还可以在电视直播中看到大楼倒塌。

sentences.en: And we could juxtapose those individuals who said that they had seen the attacks live on television, as compared to those who did not.
sentences.zh: 我们可以将那些说自己在电视上看过袭击直播的人与那些没有看过的人进行对比。

sentences.en: We found that those who did witness the events of 9-11 live on television were more likely to be exhibiting stress responses, both psychological and physical stress responses,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，那些在电视直播中亲眼目睹“9·11”事件的人更有可能表现出压力反应，包括心理和生理压力反应，

sentences.en: and more likely to develop physical health complaints over the next three years.
sentences.zh: 并且更有可能在接下来的三年里出现身体健康主诉。

sentences.en: Let me say one very important part of our study, because it was a longitudinal study, that is, we repeatedly studied the same individuals over time,
sentences.zh: 请允许我指出我们研究中非常重要的一点，因为这是一项纵向研究，也就是说，我们随着时间的推移反复研究相同的个体，

sentences.en: we could explore the development of physical health complaints.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以探究身体健康主诉的发展过程。

sentences.en: So we know where they were physically and psychologically before the attacks, we had data that were collected on those individuals,
sentences.zh: 因此我们了解他们在袭击发生前的身体和心理状况，我们掌握了这些收集到的个人数据，

sentences.en: and we could monitor the new onset of psychological and physical concerns.
sentences.zh: 并且我们可以监测心理和身体问题的新发情况。

sentences.en: It is also the case that because we began our study within a few days after the 9-11 attacks, we were not asking people to reconstruct their memory of where they were at that time.
sentences.zh: 同样由于我们在“9·11”袭击后几天内就开始了研究，我们并不是让人们去重建他们当时所在位置的记忆。

sentences.en: We were actually measuring that about five days after the attacks.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上是在袭击发生后大约五天对其实际进行测量。

sentences.en: And so we could say, how many hours over the past week have you spent watching media, as opposed to me asking you 20 years later, how many hours do you think you were spending?
sentences.zh: 因此我们可以问：“在过去的一周里，你花了多少个小时看媒体报道？”而不是在20年后问你：“你觉得你当时花了多少个小时？”

sentences.en: I will say that of our nationally representative sample of individuals, about 60% reported within those, within a few days after the 9-11 attacks,
sentences.zh: 我要说的是，在我们具有全国代表性的样本中，大约60%的人在“9·11”袭击发生后的几天内报告说，

sentences.en: that they did witness some portion of the attacks live on television.
sentences.zh: 他们确实在电视直播中目睹了袭击的一部分。

sentences.en: So it was about 60%, so it was about 60% witnessed either the second plane hitting the World Trade Center or the building's fall,
sentences.zh: 所以大约是60%，即大约60%的人目睹了第二架飞机撞击世贸中心或大楼倒塌，

sentences.en: and about 40% learned about the attacks afterwards.
sentences.zh: 大约40%的人是在事后才得知这些袭击的。

sentences.en: In our sample, we had about 5% of individuals who were either in New York or Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 在我们的样本中，大约有5%的人当时身处纽约、华盛顿特区

sentences.en: or Pennsylvania, or had been on the phone with somebody in one of the buildings, or had been in the area and had witnessed the events directly.
sentences.zh: 或宾夕法尼亚州，或者曾与其中一栋大楼里的人通电话，或者当时就在该地区并直接目睹了事件。

sentences.en: So here we are 20 years later.
sentences.zh: 20年后的今天，我们迎来了这一节点。

sentences.en: Do you think that as a country, we're still feeling the effects of 9-11 today, or has it receded in our minds by now?
sentences.zh: 你认为作为国家，我们今天是否仍能感受到“9·11”的影响，还是说它现在已经在我们心中淡去了？

sentences.en: You know, it's very, very difficult to say, because so many aspects of our society have changed over the last 20 years.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这非常非常难说，因为在过去的20年里，我们社会的许多方面都发生了变化。

sentences.en: During the 9-11 attacks, the main way in which people learned about tragic events was via television.
sentences.zh: 在“9·11”袭击期间，人们了解悲剧事件的主要途径是通过电视。

sentences.en: We also, of course, had radio and print media.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们当时也有广播和平面媒体。

sentences.en: But now, 20 years later, we learn about events across the world in seconds because of a very different media landscape.
sentences.zh: 但现在，20年过去了，由于截然不同的媒体格局，我们在几秒钟内就能了解世界各地发生的事件。

sentences.en: So the world has changed, has gotten smaller in some ways because of the easy access to content across the world.
sentences.zh: 因此世界变了，由于能够轻松获取全球内容，它在某些方面变得更小了。

sentences.en: Many other things have changed simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 许多其他事情也同时发生了变化。

sentences.en: It's very difficult to link those societal changes to the 9-11 attacks directly.
sentences.zh: 很难将这些社会变化直接与“9·11”袭击联系起来。

sentences.en: However, those who are old enough to remember prior to 9-11 also remember that one used to be able to go through the airport without any barriers.
sentences.zh: 然而，那些年龄大到足以记事、经历过“9·11”之前的人也记得，过去人们过机场安检时没有任何障碍。

sentences.en: You could run to your plane 10 minutes before the plane, and I used to do that quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 你可以在飞机起飞前10分钟跑向登机口，我过去经常这样做。

sentences.en: I hated to be in the airport more than 10 minutes before my plane.
sentences.zh: 我讨厌在飞机起飞前10分钟以上到达机场。

sentences.en: We now stand in long lines without protest prior to going to an airport gate,
sentences.zh: 现在我们毫无怨言地排着长队通过机场登机口，

sentences.en: and those of us who are old enough to remember previously do that now without any protest because we very much remember the events of 9-11.
sentences.zh: 而我们这些年龄大到足以记得过去的人现在这样做也毫无怨言，因为我们深深地记住了“9·11”事件。

sentences.en: The entire Department of Homeland Security grew out of 9-11.
sentences.zh: 整个国土安全部就是从“9·11”中诞生的。

sentences.en: The concern about terrorism was relatively non-existent in the United States prior to the 9-11 attacks.
sentences.zh: 在“9·11”袭击之前，美国对恐怖主义的担忧几乎是不存在的。

sentences.en: So there are so many things that have changed over the last several decades, and it's very,
sentences.zh: 所以在过去的几十年里，有太多的事情发生了变化，要将其与

sentences.en: very difficult to link it to the events of those days or the events of the few years later.
sentences.zh: 那些天的事件或几年后的事件联系起来，是非常非常困难的。

sentences.en: We've also become more polarized in our country politically.
sentences.zh: 我们在国家的政治上也变得更加两极分化。

sentences.en: The onset of social media has changed the way in which we communicate with one another.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体的兴起改变了我们彼此交流的方式。

sentences.en: All of those things have coincidentally changed during those two decades.
sentences.zh: 在这二十年里，所有这些事情都巧合地发生了变化。

sentences.en: So I find it difficult to link those directly to 9-11.
sentences.zh: 所以我发现很难将这些直接与“9·11”联系起来。

sentences.en: I think that's really the role of historians.
sentences.zh: 我认为这其实是历史学家扮演的角色。

sentences.en: As a psychologist, I'm not a historian.
sentences.zh: 作为心理学家，我不是历史学家。

sentences.en: I can't speak to the historical impact of the events of those days.
sentences.zh: 我无法谈论那些日子里事件的历史影响。

sentences.en: I certainly know that there are just many differences in our society in the last 20 years.
sentences.zh: 我当然知道，在过去的20年里，我们的社会确实存在很多差异。

sentences.en: In effect, these are reminders that are with us every day, except that what you're saying is that we're not making the associations.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这些都是每天都在提醒我们的事物，只不过你的意思是，我们没有把它们联系起来。

sentences.en: So it has become normal life to take our shoes off and go through metal detectors and everything else that we have to do today.
sentences.zh: 因此，脱鞋、过金属探测器以及今天我们必须做的所有其他事情，都成了日常生活的一部分。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And there's no proteSt.
sentences.zh: 而且毫无怨言。

sentences.en: Similarly, when young people go to concerts, they open up their handbags, women open up their handbags, men are used to, were used to going through metal detectors.
sentences.zh: 同样，当年轻人去听音乐会时，他们会打开手提包，女性打开手提包，男性习惯了、过去习惯了通过金属探测器。

sentences.en: That just didn't happen decades ago.
sentences.zh: 几十年前根本没有这种事。

sentences.en: It didn't happen before 9-11.
sentences.zh: 在“9·11”之前也没有发生过。

sentences.en: All of those changes were in direct response to a concern for terrorism on our soil.
sentences.zh: 所有这些改变都是对我们本土遭受恐怖主义威胁的直接回应。

sentences.en: Let me ask you a related question.
sentences.zh: 让我问你一个相关的问题。

sentences.en: Why is it important to mark anniversaries of tragic events?
sentences.zh: 为什么纪念悲剧事件的周年日很重要？

sentences.en: Do these bring back the trauma or do they help people process and cope with it or both?
sentences.zh: 这些纪念活动是会勾起创伤，还是会帮助人们处理和应对创伤，亦或是两者兼有？

sentences.en: That's a very interesting question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的问题。

sentences.en: One of the things that I think is really clear is inadvertently the media and even interviews like this bring forward again these events.
sentences.zh: 我认为非常明显的一点是，媒体甚至像这样的采访会无意中再次把这些事件呈现在人们面前。

sentences.en: I personally have been very unhappy to see images of the 9-11 attacks, graphic images of the 9-11 attacks portrayed in the media.
sentences.zh: 我个人非常不高兴在媒体上看到“9·11”袭击的画面，即“9·11”袭击的血腥直观画面被呈现出来。

sentences.en: And for many years on the 9-11 anniversary, we would see pictures of the World Trade Center either on fire or people running through the streets and filled with soot or people...
sentences.zh: 并且多年来在“9·11”周年纪念日上，我们会看到世贸中心着火的照片，或者人们满身灰烬地跑过街道，或者人们……

sentences.en: Jumping out of windows.
sentences.zh: 从窗户跳下。

sentences.en: Jumping out of windows.
sentences.zh: 从窗户跳下。

sentences.en: Although those images were not shown in the early years.
sentences.zh: 尽管这些画面在早期并没有播放。

sentences.en: In fact, there were a number of editorial decisions made by the media not to show some of those graphic images in the days and weeks after 9-11.
sentences.zh: 事实上，媒体在“9·11”发生后的几天和几周内做出了许多编辑决定，不播放其中一些血腥的画面。

sentences.en: I personally have preferred seeing images of, there's some beautiful images of blue lights coming up where the World Trade Center had been.
sentences.zh: 我个人更喜欢看到一些画面，比如世贸中心原址上升起蓝色灯光的优美画面。

sentences.en: Beautiful memorials to the loved ones that people loSt.
sentences.zh: 对失去亲人的优美纪念。

sentences.en: Those are very different from the images of the tragedy.
sentences.zh: 这些与悲剧的画面截然不同。

sentences.en: So, I think it's very difficult for us to avoid remembering the tragedy when there are so many media portrayals of the tragedy that we see over and over again.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为当我们在媒体上一次又一次地看到那么多悲剧的影像时，要避免记住这场悲剧对我们来说非常困难。

sentences.en: I think, of course, that for any anniversary, anniversaries of positive events like birthdays or weddings or anniversaries of tragic events like 9-11 or the loss of a loved one,
sentences.zh: 我认为，当然对于任何周年纪念来说，无论是生日或婚礼等积极事件的周年纪念，还是“9·11”或痛失亲人等悲剧事件的周年纪念，

sentences.en: we, of course, think about the events on those days.
sentences.zh: 我们当然都会在那些日子里想起这些事件。

sentences.en: I don't think in any way that anybody would advocate that.
sentences.zh: 我不认为任何人会以任何方式主张这一点。

sentences.en: We try to forget.
sentences.zh: 我们试图去忘记。

sentences.en: Of course, we want to memorialize those who we lost, and we want to be vigilant so that the kinds of events that we're talking about don't occur again.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们希望缅怀那些逝去的人，我们希望保持警惕，以便我们所谈论的那类事件不再发生。

sentences.en: Let's switch gears and talk about the collective traumas that many people have experienced in the last year, year and a half.
sentences.zh: 让我们转换一下话题，谈谈许多人在过去一年、一年半里经历的集体创伤。

sentences.en: You wrote an article earlier this year called Coping with Cascading Collective Traumas in the United States.
sentences.zh: 你今年早些时候写过一篇文章，名为《在美国应对层层叠加的集体创伤》。

sentences.en: Can you explain that term, cascading collective traumas?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下“层层叠加的集体创伤”这个词吗？

sentences.en: How unprecedented is the year we've just had?
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚过去的这一年是多么史无前例？

sentences.en: Well, I started to think about the cascade of traumatic events that we, as a country,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我开始思考作为国家所经历的层叠创伤事件，

sentences.en: were dealing with the morning after I learned of George Floyd's untimely and tragic murder in May, I believe it was, of 2020.
sentences.zh: 那是2020年5月（如果我没记错的话），在得知乔治·弗洛伊德不幸遇害的第二天早晨。

sentences.en: And I was actually lying in bed thinking about it in the morning, how terrible a year it had been.
sentences.zh: 那天早晨我实际上正躺在床上思考这件事，觉得这是多么糟糕的一年。

sentences.en: We began, of course, with the recognition of COVID.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们是从认识新冠疫情开始的。

sentences.en: It wasn't actually called it was called the novel coronavirus in the early in the early days.
sentences.zh: 当时其实还不叫这个，在早期它被称为新型冠状病毒。

sentences.en: And the widespread quarantines that were initiated across the world, or certainly in the United States,
sentences.zh: 全球各地、或者至少在美国各地启动了广泛的隔离，

sentences.en: and the economic fallout from that and the millions of people who were losing their jobs at that time.
sentences.zh: 以及由此带来的经济影响和当时数百万失去工作的人。

sentences.en: And I thought about how these events led people to have a lot of time on their hands, more time on their hands than they, for many people,
sentences.zh: 我想到这些事件让人们有了大量的空闲时间，对许多人来说比他们以往更多的空闲时间，

sentences.en: those who were certainly not the essential workers who were still working very hard to keep our country going.
sentences.zh: 当然，那些仍在努力工作以维持我们国家运转的Essential workers（核心基本岗位工作者）除外。

sentences.en: But I realized that people had a lot of time on their hands, both to watch television or engage in media, social media.
sentences.zh: 但我意识到人们有大量的空闲时间，既可以看电视，也可以参与媒体和社交媒体。

sentences.en: And so we were sort of primed to hear about the events or the murder of George Floyd in ways that I think we had been, many people had been aware of,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们已经做好了心理准备去了解乔治·弗洛伊德遇害的事件，以一种我认为许多人之前虽有所觉察，

sentences.en: but not really focused on in the way that we were in the context of this terrible pandemic.
sentences.zh: 但并未真正像在这次可怕的大流行背景下那样去关注的方式。

sentences.en: Around the same time, certainly in the couple of weeks and months after George Floyd's murder, we had wildfires throughout the NorthweSt.
sentences.zh: 大约在同一时期，当然在乔治·弗洛伊德遇害后的几周和几个月内，西北地区发生了山火。

sentences.en: There were increased numbers of hurricanes that had not been, I believe 2020 was, if not the worst, one of the worst years on record for hurricanes in the United States.
sentences.zh: 飓风数量也有所增加，我相信2020年即使不是最糟糕的一年，也是美国有记录以来飓风灾害最严重的一年之一。

sentences.en: And all of this just seemed almost too much to bear.
sentences.zh: 这一切似乎让人几乎难以承受。

sentences.en: So my colleagues, Alison Holman and Dana Garfin and I wrote a paper, as you said, called Cascade, Coping with Cascading Collective Traumas in the United States,
sentences.zh: 因此，正如你所说，我的同事艾莉森·霍尔曼（Alison Holman）、达娜·加芬（Dana Garfin）和我写了一篇论文，题为《在美国应对层层叠加的集体创伤》，

sentences.en: in which we highlighted the important role of both direct exposure to these kinds of experiences, as well as indirect exposure via the media.
sentences.zh: 我们在其中强调了直接接触这些经历以及通过媒体进行间接接触的重要作用。

sentences.en: And we argued how important it was for people to monitor their exposure to media about tragedies.
sentences.zh: 我们主张，人们密切关注自己接触关于悲剧的媒体报道是多么重要。

sentences.en: And we acknowledged that it was going to be a very difficult year to come out of.
sentences.zh: 我们也承认，要走出这艰难的一年将会非常不易。

sentences.en: I have been thinking a lot about interviews and talks that I gave in the early days after the pandemic began.
sentences.zh: 我一直在思考大流行初期我所做的一些采访和讲座。

sentences.en: And I said at the time that we don't know how long this pandemic is going to last and we don't know how bad it's going to get.
sentences.zh: 当时我说过，我们不知道这场大流行会持续多久，也不知道情况会变得多糟糕。

sentences.en: And in 2021, sadly, I would still say the same thing.
sentences.zh: 而令人遗憾的是，到了2021年，我依然会这么说。

sentences.en: We really don't know how bad it's going to get and we don't know how long it's going to laSt.
sentences.zh: 我们真的不知道情况会变得多糟糕，也不知道它会持续多久。

sentences.en: Of course, when I said that back in the spring of 2020, we didn't have vaccines, but now we have vaccines.
sentences.zh: 当然，当我在2020年春天说这话时，我们还没有疫苗，但现在我们有了。

sentences.en: Not everybody in the world who would love to get a vaccine has access to it.
sentences.zh: 并非世界上所有渴望接种疫苗的人都能获得疫苗。

sentences.en: And many people who have access to vaccines in our country have chosen not to get them.
sentences.zh: 而在我们国家，许多能够获得疫苗的人却选择不去接种。

sentences.en: So I think that that puts us in a very complicated situation where we don't know how long it's going to last and we don't know how bad it's going to get.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这让我们陷入了一种非常复杂的处境，我们既不知道它会持续多久，也不知道情况会变得多糟糕。

sentences.en: Given all the death, doom and destruction that's been raining down on us, I mean, do we get maxed out at some point?
sentences.zh: 鉴于这种种死亡、末日和毁灭如雨点般向我们砸来，我的意思是，我们在某个时刻会达到承受的极限吗？

sentences.en: Do we become inured to this much trauma and you just get numb or does it just pile and pile and pile up?
sentences.zh: 我们会对如此多的创伤习以为常从而变得麻木，还是这些创伤只会不断地累积叠加？

sentences.en: Well, I think that we must recognize that everybody hasn't been impacted by the pandemic in the same way.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为我们必须认识到，每个人受大流行的影响并不完全相同。

sentences.en: So there are millions and millions of individuals who have lost a loved one.
sentences.zh: 有数以千万计的人失去了亲人。

sentences.en: There are millions and millions of individuals who have gotten sick themselves.
sentences.zh: 有数以千万计的人自己染上了疾病。

sentences.en: And there are some who have been fortunate because of their economic circumstances or just luck, or perhaps because of vigilance that have been personally untouched by the events,
sentences.zh: 还有一些人由于经济状况、纯粹的运气，或者是因为保持警惕，而十分幸运地在个人层面上没有受到这些事件的影响，

sentences.en: except that they are spending more time at home.
sentences.zh: 除了他们花在在家里的时间变多了。

sentences.en: Maybe they're gardening.
sentences.zh: 也许他们在园艺。

sentences.en: I mean, the range of exposures and the range of impact of the pandemic has really differed.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，大流行带来的接触范围和影响范围确实千差万别。

sentences.en: It's no secret that there are certain groups, in particular Native American groups, Latinx individuals,
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，某些群体，特别是美洲原住民群体、拉丁裔个人、

sentences.en: Black residents who have been more impacted by the illness and the deaths as a result of COVID than others.
sentences.zh: 黑人居民，受新冠引起的疾病和死亡的影响比其他人更大。

sentences.en: So we have to recognize it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们必须认识到这一点。

sentences.en: It hasn't been a one-size-fits-all exposure, and there will not be a one-size-fits-all response.
sentences.zh: 这不是一种“一刀切”的接触，也不会有一种“一刀切”的应对方式。

sentences.en: I've been studying tragedy for over 40 years, and the most important message that I learned back when I was working on my dissertation, and now 40 years later, is that there is not
sentences.zh: 我研究悲剧已经超过40年了，我在当年做博士论文时学到的最重要的信息，以及40年后的今天我所认识到的是，并不存在

sentences.en: a one-size-fits-all response.
sentences.zh: 一种“一刀切”的应对方式。

sentences.en: There's enormous variability in how people process and respond to events, very much influenced by
sentences.zh: 人们对事件的处理和反应存在着巨大的差异，这在很大程度上受到

sentences.en: people's prior life experiences, by their chronic stress or their experiences during the event, and by the amount of support and resources that they have in the aftermath.
sentences.zh: 人们先前的人生经历、慢性压力或在事件期间的经历，以及他们在事后拥有的支持和资源量的影响。

sentences.en: All of this is to say it's a complicated situation, and that's why we try to collect data, why we try to do research on this topic.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都说明情况很复杂，这就是为什么我们要收集数据，为什么我们要在这个课题上进行研究。

sentences.en: My colleagues and I, for many, many years, have tried to conduct methodologically rigorous systematic research on these kinds of issues.
sentences.zh: 多年来，我和我的同事们一直试图对这类问题进行方法论严谨的系统性研究。

sentences.en: Of course, it depends on getting others to share their experiences, their emotions, and their feelings, and their thoughts and concerns with us, but we have been very fortunate.
sentences.zh: 当然，这取决于能否让其他人与我们分享他们的经历、情绪、感受、想法和担忧，但我们非常幸运。

sentences.en: I've had tens of thousands of people who have participated in my studies, and I think it helps
sentences.zh: 有数以万计的人参与了我的研究，我认为这帮

sentences.en: me recognize that there is no one-size-fits-all response, and I certainly don't want to imply
sentences.zh: 助我认识到并不存在“一刀切”的应对方式，我当然不想暗示

sentences.en: that there is, in the same way that the events of 2020 have impacted people in different ways.
sentences.zh: 存在这种方式，正如2020年的事件以不同的方式影响了人们一样。

sentences.en: There's a field of study that looks at something called post-traumatic growth.
sentences.zh: 有一个研究领域探讨的是被称为“创伤后成长”的概念。

sentences.en: In some cases, people can find meaning in tragedy, and living through a traumatic time can spark positive development and personal growth.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，人们可以在悲剧中找到意义，经历创伤时期可以激发积极的发展和个人成长。

sentences.en: Is that something you've seen in your research on collective trauma?
sentences.zh: 这是你在集体创伤研究中看到的情况吗？

sentences.en: I personally see these kinds of positive benefits that people see as a coping strategy.
sentences.zh: 我个人确实看到了人们将其视为一种应对策略的这些积极益处。

sentences.en: This is the way in which people cope with this terrible adversity and uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 这是人们应对这种可怕的逆境和不确定性的方式。

sentences.en: But my colleagues and I are working on a paper right now looking at the positive experiences that have come out of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 但我和我的同事目前正在写一篇论文，探讨大流行带来的积极体验。

sentences.en: We don't use the term post-traumatic growth.
sentences.zh: 我们不使用“创伤后成长”这个词。

sentences.en: That is something that I think others may use.
sentences.zh: 我认为其他人可能会使用这个词。

sentences.en: We see these as benefits that people are able to see.
sentences.zh: 我们将这些视为人们能够看到的益处。

sentences.en: Perhaps there are mental gymnastics that people are engaging in to cope with the tragedy simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 也许人们在同时进行某种心理体操来应对这场悲剧。

sentences.en: They're acknowledging the tragedy, but they are seeing some positive experiences.
sentences.zh: 他们在承认悲剧的同时，也看到了一些积极的体验。

sentences.en: Certainly, many, many people have enjoyed the opportunity to work from home and not have to sit in traffic.
sentences.zh: 当然，许许多多的人都很享受在家工作而不必堵在路上的机会。

sentences.en: And then there are other individuals who are stuck in a residence with somebody who is abusive or somebody with whom they have a very complicated personal relationship.
sentences.zh: 但也有另一些人，他们和有虐待行为的人或关系非常复杂的人困在同一个住所里。

sentences.en: Maybe they don't have good internet.
sentences.zh: 也许他们没有好的网络。

sentences.en: Maybe they are living in an environment that makes working from home extraordinarily difficult.
sentences.zh: 也许他们所处的环境让在家工作变得异常艰难。

sentences.en: And so, while some people may find the positive benefits of not having to sit in traffic, others find that same experience to be quite stressful and quite challenging.
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然有些人可能会发现不用堵车带来的积极益处，但另一些人却觉得同样的经历相当有压力、相当具有挑战性。

sentences.en: So, I think it's important, again, to recognize that there are different ways to respond.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为再次强调认识到存在不同的应对方式是很重要的。

sentences.en: We have found that many people are able to see a somewhat silver or gray lining in the blackness and the bleakness.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，许多人在黑暗和阴霾中能够看到一丝光明或一线希望。

sentences.en: And I do see that as a very positive way to cope with this because otherwise it really can be overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为这是一种应对危机的非常积极的方式，否则它真的会让人难以承受。

sentences.en: We haven't exploited as much in our data yet, but I've been monitoring what others are reporting in data across the world.
sentences.zh: 我们还没有在数据中过多地挖掘这一点，但我一直在监测世界各地其他人在数据中报告的内容。

sentences.en: And we do know that in some communities or – and again, the data are still – it's important for us to explore more than one study.
sentences.zh: 我们确实知道，在某些社区里——而且再次说明，数据仍在——对我们来说，探索多项研究非常重要。

sentences.en: But it does look like in some communities, rates of substance use and substance abuse may have increased.
sentences.zh: 但看起来在某些社区中，物质使用和物质滥用的比率可能有所上升。

sentences.en: There have been some articles suggesting that the plague of loneliness has led to increased depression.
sentences.zh: 有一些文章表明，孤独的瘟疫导致了抑郁症的增加。

sentences.en: We've seen some of that in our own data.
sentences.zh: 我们在自己的数据中也看到了这一点。

sentences.en: I think we'll – again, we'll have to see what the consequences are.
sentences.zh: 我想我们会——同样，我们得看看后果会是什么。

sentences.en: But at the same time that people are experiencing these negative psychological states, many people are trying to hold on to some positive experiences that they've had.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，当人们经历这些消极的心理状态时，许多人也在努力坚持他们所经历的一些积极体验。

sentences.en: And I do feel that once we're out of this, I think once we are through this terrible time, I do feel quite –
sentences.zh: 我确实觉得，一旦我们摆脱了这一切，一旦我们度过了这段可怕的时期，我真的觉得——

sentences.en: I think it's likely that people will be able to look back on the events of 2020,
sentences.zh: 我认为人们很有可能会回首2020年、

sentences.en: 2021 and see that they were stronger than they had expected or that they were able to come through recognizing some skills that they didn't realize that they had.
sentences.zh: 2021年的事件，发现自己比预期的要坚强，或者他们能够通过认识到自己以前未曾察觉的某些技能来挺过难关。

sentences.en: But again, that is not to say that there will be some who will be unable to find anything positive.
sentences.zh: 但话又说回来，这并不是说有些人将无法找到任何积极的东西。

sentences.en: I mean, this has really been a terrible year.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这真的是可怕的一年。

sentences.en: And for people who have lost loved ones, who were not able to say goodbye, who were unable to have a ritual burial, all of these things are just terrible.
sentences.zh: 对于那些失去了亲人、无法好好告别、无法举行常规葬礼的人来说，所有这些事情都是极其糟糕的。

sentences.en: And I don't want – I think it's very important that we don't imply that everybody should be seeing something positive about this.
sentences.zh: 我不想——我认为非常重要的是，我们不要暗示每个人都应该从中看到积极的一面。

sentences.en: Because for some, there is nothing positive about this horrible year.
sentences.zh: 因为对有些人来说，这个可怕的年份没有任何积极可言。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think we have all suffered losses, both real and symbolic,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我认为我们都遭受了损失，无论是实质上的还是象征性的，

sentences.en: the cancellation of weddings or the inability to celebrate one senior year in high school or the inability to play sports.
sentences.zh: 取消婚礼、无法庆祝高中毕业的最后一年、或者无法进行体育运动。

sentences.en: I mean, all of these things that happened in 2020, I think, are with some people and will likely, for those individuals, never leave them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为2020年发生的这一切都伴随着一些人，而且对于那些人来说，可能永远不会离开他们。

sentences.en: And I wouldn't expect that it would.
sentences.zh: 我也不会指望它会离开。

sentences.en: You published a paper a couple of years ago about near-miss experiences that found people who narrowly missed a traumatic event were more likely to experience PTSD and survivor's guilt.
sentences.zh: 你几年前发表过一篇关于“死里逃生（险情）”经历的论文，发现险些遭遇创伤事件的人更有可能经历创伤后应激障碍和幸存者内疚。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that research?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈那项研究吗？

sentences.en: So, there was a paper that my colleague, Michael Pullen, and I wrote about near misses after 9-11.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的同事迈克尔·普伦和我写过一篇关于“9·11”事件后险情的研究论文。

sentences.en: We had – in our sample of about 3,500, we had more than 100 individuals who had either nearly missed going to New York or nearly missed getting on an airplane
sentences.zh: 在我们的约3500人的样本中，有100多个人要么差点去成纽约，要么差点登上飞机，

sentences.en: or had a family member that nearly missed the possibility of having been directly impacted by 9-11.
sentences.zh: 或者有家庭成员差点就有可能直接受到“9·11”事件的影响。

sentences.en: And I would probably say we didn't say that they experienced PTSD.
sentences.zh: 我可能会说，我们并没有说他们经历了PTSD（创伤后应激障碍）。

sentences.en: We probably indicated that they experienced some stress symptoms that are – and it's important to recognize that there is a clinical diagnosis of PTSD.
sentences.zh: 我们大概是指他们经历了一些压力症状，这是——而且必须认识到，PTSD有一个临床诊断标准。

sentences.en: PTSD that requires a clinician to make that diagnosis.
sentences.zh: PTSD需要临床医生来做出诊断。

sentences.en: And also, in the current clinical diagnostic criteria requires that people are directly exposed to a tragedy.
sentences.zh: 此外，当前的临床诊断标准要求人们直接暴露于悲剧之中。

sentences.en: So, we are, in fact, looking at the opposite, individuals who just missed experiencing a tragedy.
sentences.zh: 所以，事实上我们研究的是相反的情况，即那些刚刚好错过经历悲剧的个人。

sentences.en: So, they wouldn't really be eligible to be diagnosed with PTSD, but they were more likely to experience post-traumatic stress symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们实际上不符合被诊断为PTSD的条件，但他们更有可能经历创伤后应激症状。

sentences.en: So, there have been a few studies on near misses.
sentences.zh: 所以，关于险情的研究并不多。

sentences.en: It's a very interesting and understudied topic and one that I think will perhaps be of interest to researchers in the future as we look back on the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣且研究不足的课题，我认为在我们回顾这场大流行时，它可能会引起未来研究人员的兴趣。

sentences.en: Of course,
sentences.zh: 当然，

sentences.en: we asked people in the – I think a few months after – I think it was the second wave of data collection after the 9-11 attacks whether they had experienced a near miss and how they – to tell us a little bit about that.
sentences.zh: 我们在——我想在“9·11”袭击之后的几个月里——我认为那是第二轮数据收集时，询问了人们是否经历过险情以及他们的感受——给我们讲讲这方面的情况。

sentences.en: And, you know, it is the case that some people experience – you know, maybe they weren't going to get on the exact plane that crashed into the World Trade Center,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，确实有些人经历过——你知道，也许他们本来不会坐上那架撞向世界贸易中心的特定飞机，

sentences.en: but they were also going to get on a plane going to New York.
sentences.zh: 但他们当时也打算坐飞机去纽约。

sentences.en: I mean, all of these can lead people to recognize that they benefited by not having gotten on that airplane or by not having gone to the building and others experienced tragedy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，所有这些都会让人们认识到，他们因为没有登上那架飞机或没有去那栋大楼而获益，而其他人却遭遇了悲剧。

sentences.en: And that has been linked to a concept that is called survivor guilt, that people do feel a sense that they were lucky and that others were not so lucky.
sentences.zh: 这与一个被称为幸存者内疚的概念有关，人们确实会感到一种自己很幸运而别人没那么幸运的心态。

sentences.en: And we also found very similar psychological experiences in the early 90s among gay men who were engaged in the very same activities that led some gay men to get AIDS.
sentences.zh: 90年代初，我们在同性恋男性群体中也发现了非常类似的心理经历，他们当时从事的正是导致一些同性恋男性感染艾滋病的相同活动。

sentences.en: And these individuals were spared at random, and my colleagues and I wrote a paper about what – it was actually entitled Spared at Random,
sentences.zh: 而这些人却随机地幸免于难，我和我的同事写了一篇关于这一主题的论文——其实标题就叫《随机幸免》，

sentences.en: and it was about individuals who had really somehow by luck or good fortune just didn't contract AIDS,
sentences.zh: 讲的是那些不知怎么地靠着运气或好运而没有感染艾滋病的个人，

sentences.en: although they could report activities that they had done that had been quite similar.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们所报告的自己做过的活动相当相似。

sentences.en: But this is, of course, all before we understood how AIDS was transmitted.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这都是在我们理解艾滋病是如何传播之前发生的。

sentences.en: And they had that same feeling of guilt?
sentences.zh: 他们也有那种负罪感吗？

sentences.en: Yes, yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，是的。

sentences.en: A sense of survivor guilt.
sentences.zh: 一种幸存者内疚感。

sentences.en: It was actually – this concept of survivor guilt was formulated about individuals who survived the HolocauSt.
sentences.zh: 事实上——幸存者内疚这个概念最初是针对在大屠杀中幸存下来的人提出的。

sentences.en: And they were individuals who had been in a concentration camp but nonetheless had managed to get out and live beyond that.
sentences.zh: 他们是那些曾被关在集中营里，但最终设法逃脱并活下来的人。

sentences.en: So, you know, these are very interesting from a psychological standpoint phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，从心理学的角度来看，这些是非常有趣的现象。

sentences.en: You know, fortunately, we don't have that many opportunities to study these kinds of events.
sentences.zh: 你知道，幸运的是，我们没有那么多机会去研究这类事件。

sentences.en: But when we do, they help us understand, again, the range of exposures and the range of responses to tragedy.
sentences.zh: 但当我们有机会时，它们再次帮助我们理解了对悲剧的接触范围和反应范围。

sentences.en: So, to sum up, do you have any advice for listeners on how to cope when they're feeling stressed or anxious or overwhelmed by the cascading collective traumas of the past year?
sentences.zh: 那么总而言之，对于过去一年层出不穷的集体创伤感到压力、焦虑或不知所措的听众，您有什么应对建议吗？

sentences.en: Is there anything they can do to inoculate themselves against post-traumatic stress or anxiety?
sentences.zh: 有什么方法可以让他们免受创伤后应激或焦虑的侵扰吗？

sentences.en: Well, certainly, if individuals feel overwhelmed and unable to cope, I would encourage them and have encouraged people to reach out to clinicians.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然，如果个人感到不知所措且无法应对，我会鼓励他们并且一直在鼓励人们向临床医生寻求帮助。

sentences.en: There are hotlines that are available if people are feeling overwhelmed and feeling that they really need to connect with others.
sentences.zh: 如果人们感到不知所措，并且觉得真的很需要与他人建立联系，是有热线电话可供拨打的。

sentences.en: I think there have been new forms of mental health treatments that have moved, let's say, to telehealth, to communicate with healthcare providers virtually rather than in person.
sentences.zh: 我认为现在有了新形式的精神健康治疗，比方说转向了远程医疗，通过虚拟方式而不是面对面地与医护人员沟通。

sentences.en: But I certainly think that if individuals feel overwhelmed, they should reach out to both loved ones and to healthcare professionals, their healthcare professionals,
sentences.zh: 但我绝对认为，如果个人感到不知所措，他们应该向亲人和医疗专业人员、他们的医疗专业人员、

sentences.en: mental health professionals.
sentences.zh: 心理健康专业人员寻求帮助。

sentences.en: I also encourage people to the extent to which it's possible to monitor their media intake, to be mindful of the amount of time that they spend immersed in reading bad news.
sentences.zh: 我也鼓励人们在可能的情况下控制自己的媒体接触量，注意花在沉浸于阅读坏消息上的时间。

sentences.en: Certainly in 2020, it was all bad news all the time.
sentences.zh: 当然在2020年，满眼都是坏消息，无时无刻都是坏消息。

sentences.en: And I think it's extremely important that people recognize how much time they may be spending immersed in this bad news.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们认识到自己可能花了多少时间沉浸在这些坏消息中，这是极其重要的。

sentences.en: Journalists have called this doom scrolling.
sentences.zh: 记者们称之为“末日滚动（灾难爽刷）”。

sentences.en: I had not heard the term until some journalists contacted me to ask me what I thought about it.
sentences.zh: 直到一些记者联系我询问我对它的看法之前，我还没听说过这个词。

sentences.en: But it makes sense where somebody could sit at a computer or with a smartphone and just click on link after link after link.
sentences.zh: 但这是说得通的，一个人可能会坐在电脑前或拿着智能手机，不停地点击一个又一个链接。

sentences.en: And five hours later, they have just been immersed in reading stories about tragedy.
sentences.zh: 五个小时后，他们就一直沉浸在阅读关于悲剧的故事中。

sentences.en: So I do encourage people to monitor the amount of time that they're spending.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实鼓励人们控制自己花费的时间。

sentences.en: I am in no way advocating any kind of censorship, and I am in no way suggesting that people put their head in the sand.
sentences.zh: 我绝不是在倡导任何形式的审查制度，我也绝不是建议人们把头埋在沙子里。

sentences.en: What I'm suggesting is that people monitor the amount of time, maybe check the news at morning, noon, evening, rather than spending a lot of time reading about tragedy.
sentences.zh: 我建议的是人们控制时间，也许在早晨、中午、晚上查看新闻，而不是花大量时间阅读关于悲剧的内容。

sentences.en: And I think that recognizing that,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为认识到这一点，

sentences.en: recognizing and being mindful of one's own feelings and the need and recognition that it's appropriate to reach out to loved ones or to health care professionals or mental health professionals,
sentences.zh: 认识并留意自己的感受，意识到向亲人、医疗专业人员或心理健康专业人员寻求帮助是恰当的并予以认可，

sentences.en: as well as monitoring the amount of time that one is spent spending immersed in tragic news, I think,
sentences.zh: 同时控制花在沉浸于悲剧新闻中的时间，我认为，

sentences.en: are two very important ways in which we can cope with these very difficult times.
sentences.zh: 这是我们应对这些非常困难时期的两个非常重要的方法。

sentences.en: Excellent advice.
sentences.zh: 极好的建议。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us today, Dr. Silver, to reflect on this anniversary.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢西尔弗博士今天作客我们的节目，与我们共同回顾这个周年纪念。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: I really appreciate the opportunity.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激这个机会。

sentences.en: You can find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology at www.speakingofpsychology.org or on Apple, Stitcher, or wherever you get your favorite podcasts.
sentences.zh: 您可以在 www.speakingofpsychology.org 或在 Apple、Stitcher 以及您获取喜爱的播客的任何地方找到往期的《心理学话语》节目。

sentences.en: And please leave us a review.
sentences.zh: 请给我们留下评价。

sentences.en: If you have comments or ideas for future podcasts, you can email us at speakingofpsychology at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 如果您对未来的播客有任何意见或想法，可以发电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology at apa.org。

sentences.en: That's speakingofpsychology, all one word, at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 即 speakingofpsychology（全部连写）at apa.org。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is produced by Lee Weinerman.
sentences.zh: 《心理学话语》由李·韦内曼（Lee Weinerman）制作。

sentences.en: Our sound editor is Chris Kondayan.
sentences.zh: 我们的音频编辑是克里斯·孔达扬（Chris Kondayan）。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 谢谢收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association, I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills），代表美国心理学协会向您问候。
